System Map

Read together, the four themes are not separate pressures. Four loops connect them, and one outside switch, El Niño, acts on three of them at once. Dry years drain the buffers (R1): low storage cuts supply and drawdown lowers storage further. High prices bring more planting (B1): the food market answers a shock, a season late. The soft market corrects, late (B2): falling insurance prices let exposure grow until losses catch up. Cheap kit sells more kit (R3): falling clean-tech prices drive more installations. Arrows that cross a colour are connections no single theme carries.

LoopNameWhat it doesThis cycle
R1Dry years drain the buffers
Water		Low storage cuts the water supplied to farms and power, cuts push users onto their reserves, and drawing on reserves lowers storage further.Turning: Powell at its lowest range
B1High prices bring more planting
Food		Higher food prices bring more planting, more planting raises the harvest, larger harvests rebuild grain stocks, and larger stocks bring prices down.Turning: Brazil plants a record crop
B2The soft market corrects, late
Insurance		Falling reinsurance prices let insured value in hazard zones grow, that value raises losses after a delay, and losses push prices back up.Priming: prices still falling
R3Cheap kit sells more kit
Clean energy		Cheaper clean technology sells more of it, and more installations drive prices down further.Turning: 23 GW to Africa for $2.4bn

Hover over a status for its meaning: Turning means every step in the loop has current evidence, so it is running now; Priming means the parts are in place but the circle has not yet closed at scale.

The Scenario Matrix’s horizontal axis asks whether loop B2 (the soft market corrects, late) corrects through prices, so insurers keep carrying losses, or through insurers pulling back, so the public carries them; its vertical axis asks whether scarce goods are shared through loop B1 (high prices bring more planting), that is by markets, or whether loop R1 (dry years drain the buffers) runs far enough that governments ration.

What it means: the switch that links the four themes is El Niño: it acts on water storage, harvests and insured losses in the same year, so a firm that treats food, water and insurance as separate risks will meet them together. The levers an organisation controls are when it buys, which sites and routes it has tested against a dry year, how it uses the soft insurance market and whose clean-energy equipment it trusts.
